rows.finding: R3-2. forward-slash Windows path detection: drive-letter paths written with forward slashes, and UNC host paths written with forward slashes, evaded the leak scans in BOTH validators, which matched only the backslash spellings of the same paths. (This ledger deliberately does not spell the leak forms out: the repaired scan flags them on sight, including inside this file.)
rows.red_canary: reproduced pre-repair against the committed regexes: a drive letter followed by a colon and a FORWARD slash (both an ai-workspace path and a private-corpus path), and a forward-slash UNC host path, were ALL undetected by validate_curriculum_l1l6.SERVER_PATH_RE and validate_lesson_qualification.SERVER_RE, while the same path in backslash form was caught. The exact leak strings are not reproduced in this ledger — the repaired scan flags them, which is itself the demonstration
rows.repair: both validators gain a forward-slash scan whose lookbehinds exclude URL schemes (a drive letter is a single letter before the colon, so https:/ cannot match; forward-slash UNC requires a host segment and a further slash, so http:// and arithmetic like a // b cannot match). Two red-first mutations plus an explicit NO-FALSE-POSITIVE probe (URLs, relative paths and fractions must stay quiet) are committed in the self-test
rows.acceptance: python tools/validate_curriculum_l1l6.py --self-test (windows_drive_forward_slash_leak, unc_forward_slash_leak trip; forward_slash_no_false_positive stays quiet) && python tools/validate_lesson_qualification.py --complete
